title: The Alibi of Greywater Bay Revisited
premise: Ada Nystrom, the observant concierge of the Greywater Bay Grand Hotel, is handed a dead woman's diary by a grieving stranger—only to discover entries written after the date of her disappearance. Following the diary's coded references to hotel guests and staff, Ada uncovers a cover-up reaching into the town's founding family, whose patriarch has been quietly erasing anyone who remembers too much. With help from the stranger, who turns out to be the missing woman's estranged daughter, Ada races to decode the final entry before she becomes its next subject. In the end, Ada exposes the family's crimes at the hotel's centennial gala, chooses her found family over the institution that raised her, and finally closes the case everyone swore was closed.
about_author: Rosalind Marchetti spent fifteen years working front desks in coastal hotels before turning her eye for human behavior to fiction. She lives in a fog-bound harbor town where she collects other people's stories and returns them, slightly altered, as mysteries.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Ada Nystrom's POV. A rain-soaked stranger named Wren leaves a waterlogged diary at the desk—the property of her mother, Maren, who vanished from the hotel seven years ago. Ada notices the impossible: dated entries continuing past the disappearance. The emotional beat is quiet dread; Ada's instinct that something is wrong sharpens into obsession.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Wren POVs. They decode Maren's shorthand, finding references to hotel staff, a locked sub-basement, and the powerful Calloway family. A current employee who helps them dies in an 'accident' within hours. The beat is rising fear and guilt—Ada realizes her past successes painted a target on anyone near her.

chapters.title: What the Basement Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, then Ada's. Breaking into the sub-basement during a storm, they find Maren's final years documented: she'd been held captive by patriarch Edmund Calloway because she witnessed his son's fatal crime. They're discovered; Ada is captured while Wren escapes with the ledger. The beat is terror and sacrifice—climax begins.

chapters.title: The Centennial Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the hotel's centennial gala, Wren and Ada's found family of staff allies broadcast the ledger and Maren's recordings to every guest. Edmund unravels publicly; police arrest him and his son. Ada finds peace reading Maren's last entry—a message of hope for her daughter. The beat is catharsis, justice, and belonging.
